tagline.text: A bay of green cliffs where the Sierra Madre meets the Pacific

children.text: A coastal town at the very southern tip of Aurora province, where the Sierra Madre range drops straight into the Pacific. Grass-covered cliffs, a lighthouse, a boat-only White Beach, and sea caves have earned it the nickname "Batanes of the East," and it makes a great weekend trip of 2 days, 1 night from Manila.

Dingalan is the southernmost town on Aurora province's east coast of Luzon, bordering Quezon province across the Umiray River to the south. With no flat ground, the Sierra Madre — the Philippines' longest mountain range — drops directly into Dingalan Bay on the Pacific, so most of the town strings along a narrow coastal strip, backed entirely by dense forest and steep mountains.

It's only fairly recently that this place became known as a destination. It was once a quiet fishing village that lived mainly off logging, but photos of the grassy hills and cliffs on its seaward headland — resembling the scenery of Batanes at Luzon's northern tip — spread online and earned it the nickname "Batanes of the East." Its signature sights are the white lighthouse and viewpoint atop the cliffs, the boat-only White Beach, and Lamao Cave, carved by the waves.
Dingalan became a sub-municipality in
and a full-fledged municipality in
; it belonged to Quezon province until Aurora became its own province in
, giving Dingalan its current home. Its population is about 30,000, and tourist facilities remain modest, with homestays and small beach lodgings rather than large resorts.

It suits travelers who value scenery over amenities, and anyone who wants light trekking with both sea and mountain views. Since its sights are spread out and mostly reached by boat and on foot, touring them with a local guide over a half day to a full day is standard practice.

A white lighthouse standing on the cliffs at the tip of the headland, with grassy hills around it offering a full view of Dingalan Bay, the Sierra Madre ridgeline, and the endless Pacific. Access inside the lighthouse itself may be closed depending on the season, so plan around the outdoor scenery.

A cave and rock formation carved by waves out of the limestone coast, explored by boat to take in the blue water and cliffs. Access can be difficult on high-wave days, so follow your boatman's judgment.

A mountain waterfall reached from the village by a short tricycle ride and a short walk. You can swim in the cold pool, and recently new photo-friendly features like a bird's-nest structure and a net play area have been added.
Facing the Pacific directly, this east coast watches the sun rise straight out of the sea. Stand at the shore or the viewpoint around
to see the mountains' shadows and the sea turn color together.

children.text: Renting an outrigger boat to tour the coastal cliffs and rocky islets is one option, and the mountain drive itself over the Sierra Madre from Gabaldon is a sight worth seeing on this trip.

Ask your guide or homestay in advance, and they'll lay out a boodle fight on the beach — grilled fish, shrimp, crab, rice, and mango served on banana leaves. Going with a group makes this especially good value.

At Feeder Port, arrange a guide and an outrigger boat to tour White Beach, the lighthouse, and Lamao Cave. A round-trip boat to White Beach (about 10 people) runs around
Facing the Pacific directly on Luzon's east coast, Dingalan's weather differs from western Luzon's.
March–May
, when the sea is calmest and rain is light, is the best time for boat trips to its sights, and the grassy hills stay green during this period too.
November–February

is close to the dry season, but strong northeast monsoon winds (Amihan) bring high waves, and boats often can't sail or Lamao Cave becomes inaccessible. During this period, plan mainly around the lighthouse and viewpoint trek, which is reached on foot.
June–October
is the rainy and typhoon season, and Aurora's coast lies right in the path of typhoons making landfall. In September
, Typhoon Karding (international name Noru) made its second landfall in Dingalan and caused major damage.
Midday temperatures run about
year-round, and the viewpoint ridge has almost no shade. It's best to start trekking early in the morning and finish before midday.

Accommodation clusters in Dingalan town (the Poblacion), in Paltic near Feeder Port, and around the coastal village of Aplaya. Most are homestays and small beach resorts — a fan room runs about
a night, and an air-conditioned room or beach cottage runs about

. At White Beach you can pitch or rent a tent to camp; showers and toilets are simple, pay-per-use facilities, so bring wet wipes and a change of clothes. Rooms fill up fast during holidays and the summer peak, so it's worth contacting your accommodation ahead of time.

The food here is simple but fresh. Inihaw (grilled fish caught in Dingalan Bay), kinilaw (raw fish cured in vinegar), and steamed shrimp and crab are staples, and if you ask your guide or homestay in advance, they'll lay out a boodle fight on the beach for you. Town has only a few small karinderias (eateries), a bakery, and the public market, so bring plenty of water and snacks when heading to White Beach or the falls.
Don't throw away your environmental-fee receipt — carry it with you. It's checked again at other sites, and without it you may have to pay a second time.
The lighthouse, viewpoint, and cave often require a guide as standard practice. Arrange a guide and boat together at Feeder Port, and agree on the sites you'll visit and the total cost beforehand.
The town has almost no ATMs, and the few there are often out of order. Withdraw plenty of cash in Cabanatuan first.
Phone signal weakens once you leave Dingalan town. Download offline maps in advance.
The viewpoint ridge has no shade and coarse grass. Bring a hat, sunscreen, at least a liter of water, long pants, and shoes with good grip.
A waterproof bag keeps your camera and phone safe from sea spray during boat rides.
If you're traveling solo or as a pair, a joiner tour that splits boat and guide costs is much more economical.
If you're combining this with Baler, the usual route goes back through Cabanatuan, so plan on losing a day to travel.

Dingalan is a Pacific coast directly exposed to typhoons and the northeast monsoon. If waves run high or the coast guard halts departures, all boat-based sites are canceled, so be sure to check the weather forecast and local notices before setting out.
Many stretches around the cliffside viewpoints and lighthouse have no railing. Don't approach the edge for photos, and be especially careful on windy days.
White Beach and the coast take swells straight in from the open sea. Watch for rip currents, and don't swim far out without a life vest.
The Gabaldon–Dingalan mountain road is sometimes closed after heavy rain due to landslides and rockfalls. Check road conditions before traveling during the rainy season.
Tanawan Falls can rise suddenly after heavy rain. If the water turns murky or grows louder, get out right away.
Carry out all your trash, and don't write graffiti on the cliffs or inside the caves.
Dingalan required all tourists to carry travel insurance covering injury and death under a
